claimed_scope: Synthetic necessary resource and capacity accounting for one complete 64-GPU MoE training update under two matched rack placements, including a global clipping barrier and a declared FP32 whole-matrix Muon ownership policy. This supports no measured runtime, device fit, speedup or achieved MFU claim.
assumptions: One hypothetical complete training update uses 64 GPUs in eight 8-GPU nodes and two racks: DP2, PP4, attention TP4/CP2 and experts ETP1/EP8 are alternate views of the same stage ranks.
The same 12-layer, hidden-width-2048, sequence-2048, top-2 MoE model, routing decisions, eight microbatches per data replica and 32768 tokens per update are held fixed across the two placements.
The balanced routing policy and exact logical directed-message plan define the service screens. A separate extreme-skew ledger stresses declared allocations and ownership.

The primary schedule explicitly completes full DP allreduce before clipping and replica0 supplies every unique norm term. This is a declared schedule choice, not intrinsic to clipping. Both optimizers and publication of weights/state follow the common clipping scalar.

Hidden matrices use the declared whole-matrix Muon ownership policy with five FP32 Newton-Schulz iterations. Embeddings, output head, router and normalization gains use AdamW. The FP32 iteration is an explicit departure from the pinned reference BF16 policy.

Assumed per-direction capacities are 80 decimal GB/s per rack crossing, 40 GB/s per node off-node send service, 160 GB/s per GPU intra-node send service and 160 GB/s aggregate within-rack injected service per rack. Device-memory service is 3 TB/s per GPU; training matrix work is 500 TFLOP/s per GPU and FP32 Muon matrix work is 100 TFLOP/s per GPU.

The necessary update floor takes the maximum resource screen within each pre- or post-clipping phase and adds those two ordered phase bounds. Endpoint rates are full duplex; GB, TB and TF use decimal powers. The comparison budget is 150 ms.
The ideal 1F1B illustration uses equal unit forward/backward service and zero transfer time. Its slots and activation lifetimes are not calibrated milliseconds.

The separately labeled reduce-scatter-first alternative splits each DP2 payload into equal reduce-scatter/allgather halves, partitions unique norm terms across both replicas, and grants optimistic post-clipping allgather/optimizer overlap without asserting a feasible DAG.
limitations: No GPU workload, distributed training implementation, measured runtime, speedup, achieved MFU or device-fit result is established.

The resource maxima are necessary lower bounds, not a complete schedulable DAG or attainable runtime prediction. Finer dependencies, contention, communication latency and omitted operations can raise the time.

Norm-scalar service between the clipping phases is conservatively omitted from the ordered sum and retained in full-update payload screens. Transport headers, padding, retries and physical switch-hop expansion are excluded.

Dense matrix FLOP floors exclude normalization, softmax, GELU, AdamW scalar work, communication kernels and software overhead. Muon FLOPs are separate from training FLOPs and cannot inflate a useful-model MFU numerator.

Capacity totals sum declared tensors and some workspace maxima, but omit framework contexts, allocator reserve or fragmentation, extra library and transport workspaces, graph pools, compilation and checkpoint buffers.
Balanced service screens do not prove a worst-skew runtime. Streaming all selected expert assignments preserves the declared selected work but can add serial chunks, queues and retained activations.

The teaching-scale token budget and canonical whole-matrix optimizer owner can make optimizer work unusually large. The example does not establish convergence quality or recommend this model-to-GPU sizing.

The attention companion has a different one-sequence, one-layer, one-device workload. Its scratch bytes and transfer milliseconds are not inputs to this system budget. A ratio between the placement floors is not a measured speedup.
decision: Primary full-DP-allreduce-before-norm schedule plus FP32 single-owner attention Muon excludes BOTH at 150 ms: A 240.629308621, B 158.934281421 ms. These are declared choices, not clipping requirements or runtimes. Alternative RS-first schedule at 150 ms: A is ruled out. B is not certified feasible.
precision_note: Values are copied from the current retained reader-summary JSON, including its printed rounding. They are arithmetic outputs and chosen inputs, not observations of GPU execution.
